result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers keep every class name and computed value, and both derive the secondary button's padding with a calc on the base padding minus 1px, so button sizes still match. B also turns spacing and font sizes into tokens without rounding any values, which covers more of what was asked for consistent new components. Its --color-white is named for appearance rather than role, while A's names (on-brand, surface) are better but A leaves spacing and card font sizes as literals. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers keep every class and computed value intact and handle the secondary button's 1px border the same way, using calc() on the base padding. A goes further on the main goal by turning spacing, card font sizes and weights into tokens with step and role names, without rounding anything; its one weak name is --color-white, which describes the colour rather than its role. B uses better role names (on-brand, surface) and flags possible name collisions, but it leaves all spacing and card type values hard-coded, which works against building more components from the same values.
